exposure: Lipid profiles (triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C)
outcome: Dyslipidemia (elevated triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, reduced HDL-C)
Adverse pregnancy outcomes (cesarean delivery, preterm birth, macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycemia, lower Apgar scores)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 220 pregnant women, comprising 110 with gestational diabetes mellitus and 110 healthy controls, recruited between 2022 and 2024.
finding: The study found that dyslipidemia in GDM, characterized by specific lipid alterations, is associated with elevated TXNIP and decreased PINK1 expression, which may contribute to metabolic disturbances and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: Gestational diabetes mellitus was associated with higher rates of cesarean delivery.
